BILL NUMBER:  S5309

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in
relation to the inspection and sale of seeds, agricultural liming
materials and commercial fertilizer

 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :

The purpose of this bill is to modify the Agriculture and Markets Law
(AML) to improve certain provisions which affect the production of
agricultural commodities, concerning the inspection and sale of seeds,
agricultural liming materials and commercial fertilizer.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill would amend AML § 136(2) and (7) to make a
technical edit to the definition of "seed" and to expand the
definition of "noxious weed seeds."

Section 2 of the bill would amend AML § 136, Definitions, to add
definitions for the terms "mulch" and "mixture, mix, or mixed."

Section 3 of the bill would amend AML § 137(C)(2) to clarify a
labeling requirement for agricultural seeds.

Section 4 of the bill would amend AML § 137(D)(1) to strengthen the
labeling requirements for vegetable seeds.

Section 5 of the bill would amend AML § 137(E)(1) to strengthen the
labeling requirements for flower seeds.

Section 6 of the bill would amend AML § § 137 to add a new subdivision
I addressing combination seed and fertilizer products.

Section 7 of the bill would amend AML § 138(B) to add a new
subdivision (10) prohibiting the sale, offering or exposing for sale
of agricultural seed more than nine months from the date of the
germination test exclusive of the month of the test.

Section 8 of the bill would amend AML § 142 to clarify its language.

Section 9 of the bill would amend AML Article 9 to add a new § 143 to
provide the Commissioner with the authority to issue stop sale orders
in cases of a violation of the law.

Section 10 the bill would amend AML § 142-gg to remove the details of
the sampling method from the law; thus providing the Commissioner with
the authority to adopt methods of sampling and analysis by regulation,
based upon methods adopted by AOAC International; and to require the
Commissioner to maintain the results of analyses of agricultural
liming materials (rather than publish them) and make them available
upon request.

Section 11 of the bill would amend AML § 143(b) to clarify the
definitions of "specialty fertilizer".

Section 12 of the bill would amend AML § 143 by adding a new
subdivision t defining the term "AOAC International".

Section 13 of the bill would amends AML § 146(c) to require that a
licensee notify the Commissioner, rather than the director, of
additional distribution points for commercial fertilizer established
during the license period.



Section 14 of the bill would amend AML § 146-a to require the
Commissioner to base the methods of sampling and analysis upon methods
adopted by the AOAC International.

Section 15 of the bill would amend AML § 146-b (b) to expand the
conditions under which a commercial fertilizer shall be deemed to be
adulterated.

Section 16 of the bill would provide for an effective date 120 days
after enactment, except that regulations may be promulgated on or
before the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This bill would amend existing Agriculture and Markets Law: Article 9,
Inspection and sale of seeds; Article 9-A, Sale of agricultural liming
materials; and Article 10, Sale and analysis of commercial fertilizer.
First, the proposed changes would clarify the laws by adding
definitions for terms currently used in the industry but not defined
in law. The changes would also make the laws more consistent with the
laws of other states and with the Association of American Seed Control
Officials' Recommended Uniform State Seed Law.

Second, the amended language will align New York State with the
sampling and testing techniques used by the majority of the other
states by requiring the use of sampling and testing procedures
established by AOAC International - a globally recognized,
independent, third party, not-for-profit association that develops
voluntary consensus standards used globally to promote trade and to
facilitate public health and safety.

Third, the bill would strengthen consumer protections by requiring
vegetable and flower seed labels to include the calendar month and
year of germination tests and "sell by" dates, and by establishing
maximum allowable levels of metals in fertilizer.

Finally, the proposed changes would remove ambiguity with regard to
"stop sale" orders pursuant to the Article 9 seed law by explicitly
authorizing the Commissioner to issue "stop sale" orders when products
are found to be in violation of the law.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This is a new proposal.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
The amendments take effect 120 days after enactment, except
regulations may be promulgated on or before the effective date.

BILL NUMBER:  S5309A

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in
relation to the inspection and sale of seeds, agricultural liming
materials and commercial fertilizer

 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :

The purpose of this bill is to modify the Agriculture and Markets Law
(AML) to improve certain provisions which affect the production of
agricultural commodities, i.e., AML Articles 9, 9-A and 10 concerning
the inspection and sale of seeds, agricultural liming materials and
commercial fertilizer. The bill adds definitions of terms currently
used, but not defined in the law; makes the laws more consistent with
model laws and the laws of other states; and adds provisions to
increase consumer protections against buying sub-standard or
adulterated materials, by establishing maximum allowable levels of
metals in fertilizer. The bill also adds a specific section to the
seed law authorizing "stop sale" orders when products are found to be
in violation of the law.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill amends AML § 136(2) and (7) to make a technical
edit to the definition of "seed" and to expand the definition of
"noxious weed seeds."

Section 2 of the bill amends AML § 136, Definitions, to add
definitions for the terms "mulch" and "mixture, mix, or mixed."

Section 3 of the bill amends AML § 137(C)(2) to clarify a labeling
requirement for agricultural seeds.

Section 4 of the bill amends AML § 137(D)(1) to strengthen the
labeling requirements for vegetable seeds.

Section 5 of the bill amends AML § 137(E)(1) to strengthen the
labeling requirements for flower seeds.

Section 6 of the bill amends AML § § 137, Label requirements of all
seeds, to add a new subdivision Ito address combination seed and
fertilizer products.

Section 7 of the bill amends AML § 138(B), Prohibitions, to add a new
subdivision (10) prohibiting the sale, offering or exposing for sale
of agricultural seed more than nine months from the date of the
germination test exclusive of the month of the test.

Section 8 of the bill amends AML § 142, Implementation, to clarify its
language.

Section 9 of the bill amends AML Article 9, Inspection and Sale of
Seeds, by adding a new § 143 to provide the Commissioner with the
authority to issue stop sale orders in cases of a violation of the
law.

Section 10 the bill amends AML § 142-gg, Sampling and analyzing (AML
Article 9-A, Sale of Agricultural Liming Materials), by removing the
details of the sampling method from the law; providing the
Commissioner with the authority to adopt methods of sampling and
analysis by regulation, based upon methods adopted by an "agricultural
and food analytical standards association"; and requiring the
Commissioner to maintain the results of analyses of agricultural
liming materials (rather than publish them) and make them available
upon request.

Section 11 of the bill amends AML § 143(b), Definitions (AML Article
10, Sale and Analysis of Commercial Fertilizer), to clarify the
definitions of "specialty fertilizer".

Section 12 of the bill amends AML § 143 by adding a new subdivision t
defining the term "agricultural and food analytical standards
association."

Section 13 of the bill amends AML § 146(c), Licensing, to require that
a licensee notify the Commissioner, rather than the director, of
additional distribution points for commercial fertilizer established
during the license period.

Section 14 of the bill amends AML § 146-a, Inspection, sampling,
analysis, by removing the details of the sampling method from the law;
and providing that the Commissioner base the methods of sampling and
analysis upon methods adopted by an "agricultural and food analytical
standards association."

Section 15 of the bill amends AML § 146-b (b), Misbranded or
adulterated fertilizer, by expanding the conditions under which a
commercial fertilizer shall be deemed to be adulterated.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This bill amends existing Agriculture and Markets Law: Article 9,
Inspection and sale of seeds; Article 9-A, Sale of agricultural liming
materials; and Article 10, Sale and analysis of commercial fertilizer.
The proposed changes clarify the laws by adding definitions of terms
currently used but not defined; and the proposed changes also make the
laws more consistent with the laws of other states and with the
Association of American Seed Control Officials' Recommended Uniform
State Seed Law.

Further, the amended language will bring New York State into accord
with the sampling and testing techniques used by the majority of the
other states by requiring the use of sampling and testing procedures
established by an " agricultural and food analytical standards
association," defined as an independent, third party, not-for-profit
association that develops voluntary, globally accepted, consensus
analytic al standards and methods for ensuring quality measurements to
address the purity and safety of agricultural materials and food and
promotes global trade and public health.

Additionally, the bill would better protect consumers from buying
sub-standard or adulterated materials by requiring vegetable and
flower seed labels to include the calendar month and year of
germination tests and "sell by" dates and by establishing maximum
allowable levels of metals in fertilizer.

Finally, the proposed changes would remove ambiguity with regard to
"stop sale" orders pursuant to the Article 9 seed law by explicitly
authorizing the Commissioner to issue "stop sale" orders when products
are found to be in violation of the law.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This is a new proposal.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None expected.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
The amendments take effect 120 days after enactment, except
regulations may be promulgated on or before the effective date; and
retailers shall have ninety days from the effective date of this act
to sell through product that is subject to the provisions of the
agriculture and markets law as amended by sections 4, 5 and 7 of this
act and held in inventory on the effective date.
